item.title: Taylor Swift & Travis Kelce’s gift helps feed Nashville families
item.description: Prior to their wedding at Madison Square Garden, Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce donated $26 million to various charities. One of the notable beneficiaries was The Store, a Nashville non-profit aimed at combating food insecurity. Due to rising food costs, The Store had paused the admission of new families prior to receiving the donation. The couple's charitable efforts supported 20 local and national organizations, reflecting their deep community ties.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A US court slashed a $74.5m tax break on 310 Tennessee acres to $500,000, upholding a 40% penalty
item.description: The United States Tax Court delivered a decisive blow to Lontrac Enterprises, LLC, reducing their claimed tax deduction for a conservation easement from $74.5 million to $500,000. The ruling highlighted the partnership's failure to provide credible evidence, resulting in the imposition of a 40 percent penalty from the IRS for a gross valuation misstatement. This case illustrates the ongoing struggles faced by taxpayers involved in syndicated conservation easement transactions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California foster-care survivor's negligence lawsuit revived after abuse report allegedly ignored in 2006
item.description: In a significant legal victory, a California man has reinstated his negligence lawsuit against Alameda County, claiming failure in protecting him from abuse within the foster care system. The appeals court's decision to overturn the dismissal signifies the ongoing need for accountability in child welfare, urging scrutiny on the county's supervision practices and highlighting the necessity for enhanced protective measures for children in foster care.

item.title: 57 years after Chicago soldier recorded 8,600-word letter from Vietnam, Smithsonian preserves his voice and the sound of a passing helicopter
item.description: In March 1969, Frank A. Kowalczyk recorded an intimate 43-minute audio letter from Vietnam for his mother, sharing vivid family updates and personal experiences from his military service. The tape not only conveyed daily life but also highlighted the stark difference between his existence amidst helicopter sounds in Vietnam and his family back home.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Bailey Quinn Frank, 15, who won $25,000 for her low-cost air sampler among nearly 2,000 applicants
item.description: Bailey Quinn Frank, a 15-year-old student from Fort Lauderdale, won a $25,000 award for her innovation. She developed a low-cost device to collect airborne bacterial DNA, benefiting environmental health monitoring. Frank's project displayed differences in bacterial communities in indoor and outdoor air samples. The competition included various challenges focusing on scientific problem-solving and teamwork. Her award highlights the potential of affordable scientific approaches to address real-world challenges.

item.title: Brisbane hospital outbuilding transformed into A$4.45M home
item.description: Sold for A$4.45 million, a remarkable five-bedroom home at 24 Brisbane Street in Annerley sets a new local record. The property's past as a hospital outbuilding is complemented by Ric DeLuca's innovative renovations, showcasing a striking sawtooth roof and preserving its historical essence. The residence boasts spacious living areas and a separate guest wing, reflecting the growing interest in character-filled homes with a story.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Washington appeals court lets wife keep home despite ex-husband's mortgage concerns
item.description: In a challenging divorce case in Washington, a couple with seven children faced intricate property division concerning their home in Sequim. The court granted the wife ownership of the property, while also placing the mortgage debt on her. This ruling allowed her to maintain the home without needing to refinance, which left the husband still tied to the mortgage.

item.title: AriGameplays shares heartbreaking message after Komanche’s death as his final X post goes viral
item.description: Twitch streamer AriGameplays penned a touching tribute to her close friend Komanche, who tragically passed away on October 25 in Monterrey, Mexico. Known as Carlos Mauricio Gómez in real life, Komanche's vibrant spirit and friendship profoundly impacted Ari's life. His last post on X garnered widespread attention, showcasing his influence in the gaming community and leaving behind a memorable legacy filled with joyful moments.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Washington court upholds $75,000 for tenant exposed to paint fumes, reverses treble damages
item.description: Eric Christiansen faced a significant dilemma when paint fumes from a neighboring workshop rendered his apartment unlivable, prompting him to take legal action. Health authorities confirmed the apartment's hazardous conditions. While a trial court awarded him almost $95,904 for his suffering, an appeals court adjusted the figure to $75,000, dismantling some claims for additional damages while initiating discussions on attorney fees.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Italian farmer finds mystery seeds in attic, grows ancient ‘miracle wheat’ with seven ears on one stalk that could help crops withstand drought
item.description: In a remarkable find, Claudio Grossi, an Italian farmer, unearthed an ancient wheat variety known as Triticum turgidum, which is believed to be over a century old. This heritage wheat demonstrated impressive drought resistance compared to its modern counterparts. Experts highlight the significance of genetic diversity in crops to combat climate change impacts, further prompting research into the nutritional upsides and drawbacks of this time-honored grain in modern agriculture.

item.title: Judge Rules Trump’s Top L.A. Prosecutor Is Serving Unlawfully, Disqualifies Him From Two Cases
item.description: A federal judge has deemed Bill Essayli's appointment as U.S. attorney to be unlawful. While this ruling comes with a temporary stay, it leaves him in his position for now. This case is crucial, as it raises questions about the legitimacy of federal prosecutor appointments. The Justice Department might decide to appeal, possibly bringing the matter before the Supreme Court for a final verdict.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Rare Edward III gold ‘leopard’ coin, circulated for just seven months, sells for £70,000 after emerging from suburban home
item.description: An exquisite gold coin from the 14th century, known as a leopard, has recently fetched a staggering £70,000 at auction. Issued during the reign of King Edward III, this coin was only in circulation for seven months before its discontinuation. Although its run was brief, the leopard coins are now regarded as rare treasures, reflecting Edward III's ambitious yet unsuccessful endeavor to enhance England's monetary system.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists develop 3D cloak that hides complex objects from infrared cameras
item.description: Researchers at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Technical University of Denmark developed a thermal invisibility cloak. This cloak effectively hides complex objects from infrared cameras while managing extreme temperatures. It successfully redirected heat away from intricate shapes during testing, demonstrating its potential applications in electronics and security. Future work will focus on concealing heat-generating objects to enhance technological capabilities.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: How Alicia Keys’ charity raised $86.6M to help children with HIV
item.description: During her journey to South Africa, Alicia Keys encountered the profound effects of HIV/AIDS on families and children, which ignited her passion to co-found Keep a Child Alive in 2003. The organization has successfully raised over $86 million, benefiting millions globally by ensuring access to medical care while advocating for health, education, and human rights. Collaborations, such as with TodayTix Group, significantly amplify their mission.
